slides.title: The big idea
slides.html:
Theorem: in a parallelogram, opposite sides are equal and opposite angles are equal. Consecutive angles are supplementary.

Proof: draw diagonal AC in parallelogram ABCD. Since AB is parallel to CD, angle BAC = angle DCA; since BC is parallel to AD, angle BCA = angle DAC (alternate interior angles). With AC shared, triangle ABC is congruent to triangle CDA by ASA. CPCTC gives AB = CD, BC = DA and angle B = angle D. Consecutive angles are same-side interior angles, so they are supplementary.
